english.title: Discharge duties or fail to discharge duties so as to cause loss / destruction / damage / death / injury on ship
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the master of]_
(B)_[a seaman employed in]_

**(..SPECIFY SHIP..),

(C)_[a United Kingdom ship,]_
(D)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was in a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY PORT..),]_
(E)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was within United Kingdom waters while proceeding to a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY PORT..),]_
(F)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was within United Kingdom waters while proceeding from a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY PORT..),]_

(G)_[discharged your duties in relation to the operation of your ship or its machinery or equipment in such a manner]_
(H)_[performed a function in relation to the operation of your ship or its machinery or equipment in such a manner]_
(I)_[failed to discharge your duties in relation to the operation of your ship or its machinery or equipment properly to such an extent]_
(J)_[failed to perform a function in relation to the operation of your ship or its machinery or equipment properly to such an extent]_

as to cause or to be likely to cause

(K)_[the loss or destruction of or serious damage to the ship or its machinery, navigational equipment or safety equipment]_
(L)_[the loss or destruction of or serious damage to another ship or structure]_
(M)_[the death of or serious injury to another person]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 58(4) and (5) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.

Date and Location
the master of / seaman employed in UK ship
OR foreign ship in UK port / waters while proceeding to or from UK port
discharged/ failed to discharge duties or performed/failed to perform function in relation to ship

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove where the act alleged against the accused constituted a breach or neglect of duty that the accused took all reasonable steps to discharge that duty - section 58(6)(a)
(ii) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove that at the time of the act alleged against the accused he was under the influence of a drug taken by him for medical purposes and either that he took it on medical advice and complied with any directions given as part of that advice or that he had no reason to believe that the drug might have the influence it had - section 58(6)(b)
(iii) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove
(a) that he could have avoided committing the offence only by disobeying a lawful command, or
(b) that in all the circumstances the loss, damage, destruction, death or injury in question, or (as the case may be) the likelihood of its being caused, either could not reasonably have been foreseen by the accused or could not reasonably have been avoided by him - section 58(6)(d)
(iv) See section 58(8) for the definitions for 'breach or neglect of duty', 'duty' and 'structure'

Note that a master or seaman referred to options (D), (E) or (F) of the above wording cannot commit an offence as outlined in option (K) of the wording - section 58(7)

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
